messages:
Maria: Heads-up — saw a sharp p99 CPU spike on telemetry-exporter in hosted-prod around 14:03 UTC. Correlation looks like an inference burst from async workers: span volume jumped to ~8k spans/s for ~2m and exporter CPU p99 hit ~95%. Any ideas?

Maria: log snippet:
```
2025-11-04T14:03:12Z exporter.go:245 INFO export start spans=8123 queue_len=4096 cpu=93.2%
2025-11-04T14:03:13Z exporter.go:258 WARN exporter throttle delay=120ms reason=backpressure
2025-11-04T14:03:50Z collector.go:131 INFO batching sent=4096 time_ms=48
```

Kenji: Ack. Can you paste the collector processor/exporter config? Curious about batch/send_batch_size and queue settings. Default batch size + long timeout can make CPU spike when bursty.

Maria: Current relevant parts (prod-otelcol):
```
processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 1024
    timeout: 5s
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_mib: 2048
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: telemetry-rw:4317
    compression: gzip
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
      exporters: [otlp]
```

Jia: Two quick thoughts: 1) The exporter + gzip combo is CPU-heavy during big payload flushes. 2) For these inference workloads we get a lot of high-cardinality, short-lived spans (per-token or per-step). Tail_sampling helps but it's costly. Consider a debounce/coalesce layer in front of exporter that dedups identical span-attributes within a short window (50-200ms) per trace id — effectively a lightweight sketch-based coalescer.

Sam: +1 on gzip concern. Switching compression off lowered CPU for previous incident but increased network egress. We should try tuning batch/send_batch_size down and shorter timeout so flushes are smaller/faster: e.g., send_batch_size: 128, timeout: 200ms for the bursty stream. Also bump exporter queue_size and exporter timeout to avoid backpressure loops.

Tasha: We also saw high CPU when spans per trace explode due to instrumented function-call spans. Can we add a server-side deterministic sampling rule: if a trace has >N spans in T seconds, apply 1/N sampling on subsequent spans in that trace? That avoids blowing up batch sizes.

Kenji: We can implement two lines of defense: 1) In Collector: memory_limiter + smaller batch + exporter queue tuning. 2) In instrumentation/SDK: lightweight debounce and span coalescing (same name + attrs) with configurable window. Fallback: tail_sampling to keep a subset of traces.

Maria: Made a quick dashboard query to validate span bursts (Prometheus):
```
sum by (job) (increase(otel_collector_exporter_spans_sent_total[1m]))
node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}  # correlate with exporter host
```
Link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/telemetry/otel-exporter (prod-panel)

instrumentation-bot: alert: telemetry-exporter-cpu-high fired 1850123456; severity=page; hosts=[collector-prod-1,collector-prod-2] :rotating_light:

Sam: Quick experiment plan:
- (now) reduce batch.send_batch_size -> 128 and timeout -> 200ms on a canary collector (collector-canary-5) :wrench:
- (5m) disable exporter gzip on canary to compare CPU/egress :chart_with_downwards_trend:
- (30m) deploy a small debounce processor binary (feature-flagged) to coalesce identical spans for 100ms window
- (post) evaluate p99 cpu, exporter queue drops, and egress delta
Assigning: @Kenji to change canary config, @Jia to prototype debounce logic, @Sam to run metric comparison, @Tasha to draft sampling fallback rules.

Tasha: Will document sampling rules and a small note for SDK teams so we can opt-in for token-level spans.

Maria: Thanks — let's keep updates here. If canary shows improvement, we’ll roll to prod and open a short RFC for a persistent debounce processor and sampling rules. :thumbsup:
